segments.text: Eight fifty-seven. Forty vendor PDFs in the inbox. Open one. Copy the vendor, the date, the total, every line.
Switch to the ERP. Remember the account code for this supplier. Fix the VAT. Then hunt the purchase order. It is not on the PDF. Enter it. Save the file. One invoice done. Thirty-nine left.
The typing is the small part. The switching is the cost. PDF to ERP. Codes to remember. POs to find. Files to file.
This flow takes one upload and carries the whole loop. It reads the receipt. Codes every line to the chart of accounts. Logs the ledger. Files the copy.
The ledger here is an ActivePieces table standing in for Xero, QuickBooks, or Sage. Same fields. Wired to your accounting tool in a real build.
Let's run it with a real invoice. Upload it. Submit.
It is reading now. Vendor, lines, amounts. Coding each line to its account. About thirty seconds in production. Sped up here.
Receipt captured. Vendor, date, amount, category. Every line coded and logged to the ledger.
One upload. Captured, coded, logged. No copying. No ERP hopping. No PO hunting. Nothing to file.
If this is your Monday, send me a DM.
